assumptions: The R-419 conditional law is positive and normalized and the projected conductance is symmetric and nonnegative.
The R-421 tail Lyapunov floor and R-422 block-mean-zero split are reused exactly on the finite Q3 rows.
The transformed cross block is the conductance block divided by sqrt(pi_i pi_j), with no diagonal contribution between disjoint supports.
Directed boundary rates are finite and computed from the same conductance normalization as R-419.
The Lean lane is a scalar algebraic cross-check, not a formalization of the finite matrix eigensolver.
boundary: R-423 closes the finite edgewise capacity inequality and records the resulting Q3 sufficient-budget boundary. It does not close the Q3LOCK common-alpha or broken-sector coercivity parents.
evidence_level: T0 / exact finite edgewise Cauchy envelope plus executed Q3-row capacity diagnostic; no uniform theorem or physical conclusion
missing_assumptions: A cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform analytic bound on both directed capacities on one Hamiltonian common core.
A positive capacity reserve after combining the capacity envelope with the core and tail floors at all scales.
A controlled two-dimensional block-mean coarse Schur sector and its interaction with the residual reserve.
Two-sided form-norm control of actual R-399 histories and a common split-limit map.
Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS/GNS identification and a sectorwise coercive estimate.
non_claims: No cutoff-, volume-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform capacity estimate.
No global Poincare or full coarse Schur theorem.
No common Hamiltonian core or split-limit dynamics.
No OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction or sectorwise spectral gap.
No continuum, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.
